title: Hypothesis-first A/B runway with adaptive exposure, shadow staging, and auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a production-ready A/B experiment scaffold focused on hypothesis-first experiments for model versions. The feature provides: 1) an experiment builder that ties a clear hypothesis + primary metric to a model variant; 2) adaptive exposure ramps that compute safe incremental exposure per cohort based on observed signals; 3) non-invasive shadow staging so model variants can be exercised without affecting user experience; 4) sequential statistical checks (frequentist alpha-spending + Bayesian drift signals) and a deterministic auto-rollback policy with safe-fallback to the control model.
motivation: Teams deploying model upgrades need a repeatable way to validate quality in production while bounding user risk and cost. Existing rollout hooks are ad-hoc; this framework should reduce incidents caused by silent regressions and shorten time-to-confidence for model deploys.
scope: Console experiment UI + API for programmatic creation, routing layer changes to support shadowing and cohort-level exposure, metrics ingestion for experiment evaluation, statistical engine for sequential checks, auto-rollback orchestration and post-mortem hooks. MVP excludes multi-armed bandit optimization and long-running cohort-specific personalization experiments (phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: Create experiment via Console or API specifying hypothesis, primary metric, control model, variant model(s), initial exposure schedule, and cohort selectors.
Routing: support 0% shadow (observe-only) and partial exposure levels per cohort with consistent hashing to user keys.
Adaptive exposure: system recommends next exposure step after a minimum observation window using risk score computed from composite metric and variance estimate.
Statistical checks: sequential monitoring using an alpha-spending function (O'Brien-Fleming style) and a Bayesian credible interval check for drift. Configurable thresholds per experiment.

Auto-rollback: when a configured statistical trigger fires, the platform automatically reduces exposure to 0% for the variant and routes traffic to the control, emits alerts and creates a rollback event in the Console.
Shadow staging: variants can be run in shadow mode with telemetry captured to experiment metrics without affecting response delivery.
Observability: experiment dashboard shows per-cohort metrics, exposure timeline, statistical test traces, and decision rationale (why we rolled back or continued).
Security: experiment definitions and telemetry respect tenant isolation and data residency rules; no sensitive payloads are stored in product-level logging unless explicitly enabled.
End-to-end test: run a synthetic smoke experiment that demonstrates a harmless regression injected into the variant and confirm auto-rollback triggers under configured thresholds.
tasks: PM: finalize hypothesis-first UX wireframes and example templates (control + single variant + multi-metric composite).
Design: provide Console screens for experiment builder, exposure timeline editor, and post-mortem summary card (Figma link in comments).
ENG (runtime): add routing flags for shadow mode and cohort exposure, ensure KV-cache and batching unaffected by observe-only runs.
ENG (telemetry): add experiment tags to metric events, ensure low-latency ingestion pipeline for near-real-time sequential checks.
ENG (stats): implement alpha-spending sequential test + Bayesian credible interval check library; expose test results via an experiment API.
ENG (orchestration): implement auto-rollback playbook with immediate fallback path and grace period to avoid flapping.
DX/Docs: write playbook and runbook that explains hypotheses, thresholds, interpreting sequential stats, and recommended rollout cadence.
QA: create synthetic experiments and run end-to-end smoke tests across Dedicated and Private deployments.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy metrics early in ramps could cause false rollbacks. Mitigation: require minimum sample sizes and use conservative alpha spending; add manual review hold for P0 customers.
Risk: shadowing doubles inference cost for variants. Mitigation: provide cost-estimate UI and allow sampling of shadow traffic (e.g., 10% of control requests).
Risk: inconsistent hashing across runtimes could leak cohort definitions. Mitigation: standardize hashing library and pin version in SDKs; runtime test-suite for consistent assignment.
Risk: regulatory constraints for Private/VPC customers. Mitigation: provide a "minimal telemetry" mode that only sends aggregated metrics to the control plane and supports on-prem stats engine.

review_feedback: Sanjay (Eng): prefer conservative defaults for initial exposure steps: 0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%.
Marta (Design): make hypothesis + primary metric required to reduce ambiguous experiments.
Omar (SRE): add circuit-breaker for system-level errors so experiments do not exacerbate capacity issues.
Legal: require opt-in for telemetry recordings containing PII; default to aggregated metrics only.
